title: Investigate and remediate per-customer generation drift after sampling-default switch affecting stop-sequence behavior
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
Multiple customers reported sudden quality regressions in prompt/eval outputs after last-week runtime change that adjusted sampling defaults and unified sampling paths across runtimes. Symptoms include: extra tokens after expected stop sequences, truncated structured responses, and higher variance in deterministic evals. This is customer-facing across Hosted and also surfaced in Dedicated and Private deployments where customers reported failing eval suites after upgrading runtime images.

Initial hypothesis and scope:
- The change introduced a new default sampling path (enable_sampling=true) to harmonize downstream behavior. Some customers implicitly relied on previous determinism/greedy behavior and exact stop-sequence truncation semantics.
- Stop-sequence detection is performed on tokenized output. Differences in tokenizer/version between model variants (and between runtime vs. SDK tokenizers) led to mismatches: stop strings that previously matched at token boundaries no longer matched after the sampling path change, allowing extra tokens to be emitted.
- The issue is not solely model-specific: Hosted customers on the unchanged model catalog saw regressions due to runtime parameter defaults. Dedicated/Private customers who upgraded images to the new runtime also saw the same failures.

What we've done so far (timeline):
- 2025-02-18: PagerDuty page triggered by Sales escalation (customer A: AcmeChat). Created this ticket and triaged P0.
- 2025-02-18: Captured failing prompts and eval sets from three customers (AcmeChat, FinTrust, DocuAgent). Artifacts uploaded.
- 2025-02-19: Reproduced locally against runtime-1.19.1 with sampling flag both on/off; confirmed stop-sequence mismatch when sampling path enabled.
- 2025-02-20: Root-cause analysis: tokenization boundary differences + change of default sampling mode combined to let sampling produce partial matches that bypass stop detection.
- 2025-02-21: Rolled a temporary runtime toggle in Hosted to restore legacy stop-token behavior for all production traffic (hotfix rollout ID: HF-2025-02-21-01). Reduced customer errors by ~95%.
- 2025-02-22: Prepared patch (PR #4521) to introduce explicit compatibility flags and fix stop-sequence canonicalization.

Root cause (concise):
The runtime change that unified sampling execution paths also changed when and how outputs are tokenized for stop-sequence comparison. In the new path, stop detection ran on a post-processed token stream that used a different tokenization boundary for multi-byte characters and whitespace sequences. Customers relying on literal stop strings (e.g., "

END
") experienced misses because those strings were split across token boundaries in the new path. The result: generators emitted extra tokens past the expected stop, breaking parsers and evals.

Proposed permanent fixes (scope & plan):
1) Compatibility guard: Add request-level and API-key-level compat flag (stop_matching_mode = legacy | strict | normalized). Default for existing API keys must remain legacy for 30 days, new keys default to normalized. This avoids surprise regressions.
2) Stop canonicalization library: Implement a lightweight normalization step that maps stop sequences into canonical token-boundary-aware representations prior to runtime comparison. This will be the long-term approach and kept consistent across SDKs.
3) SDK mapping: Update official SDKs to include mapping helpers so client-side prompts that rely on string-based stops are converted to canonical forms before being sent.
4) Dedicated/Private upgrades: Ship patched runtime image for Dedicated/Private (runtime-1.19.2) and provide an opt-in compatibility image (runtime-1.19.2-compat) for customers to validate. Provide clear upgrade notes.
5) Tests: Add a regression suite with per-customer prompt sets (captured from customers, anonymized) and include stop-edge-cases (unicode whitespace, emoji, punctuation splits). Add model-variant tokenization matrix tests.
6) Observability: Add a dashboard metric for "stop_mismatch_rate" and an alert when it spikes.

Short-term mitigations already applied:
- Hosted: rolled toggle to restore legacy stop semantics (HF-2025-02-21-01).
- Dedicated/Private: notified existing customers in 24h and recommended holding image upgrades; provided guidance to set runtime env STOP_MATCH_MODE=legacy on their images.

Open work items (this ticket covers):
- Implement compatibility guard and canonicalization (backend change).
- Push PRs for SDK helpers (JS + Python).
- Bake and publish runtime-1.19.2 and compat image.
- Add regression tests & integrate to CI.
- Draft customer comms and run legal/CS review.
- Postmortem and runbook updates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stop canonicalization implemented and covered by unit + integration tests.
- Compatibility flag implemented; existing API keys continue legacy behavior for 30 days by default.
- Hotfix is reverted on Hosted once new runtime is deployed and button-tested in canary.
- Dedicated/Private images built, smoke-tested, and docs updated.
- Regression suite included in CI and a dashboard for stop_mismatch_rate is live.
- Customer communications sent to impacted customers and CS replies tracked.

Communication artifacts and links (internal):
- Repro artifacts (prompts & eval diffs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-prompts
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1198
- Runtime patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
- Confluence postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Stop+Sequence+Compatibility+Postmortem
- Customer draft email (internal): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1example-draft
- Incident runbook entry created: IR-2025-02-21-STOP

Notes and trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Force immediate global rollback of the sampling-default change. Pros: fastest customer relief. Cons: loses intended sampling improvements and could re-introduce other variability; risky across Dedicated/Private.
- Option B (chosen): Guard + canonicalization + staged rollout. Pros: minimizes customer impact and preserves new code path benefits long-term; allows opt-in validation. Cons: more engineering work and interim complexity (compat flags).

Next immediate steps (owner: Marcus Huang):
- Merge runtime patch PR and start canary deploy to 10% of Hosted traffic (target 2025-02-25).
- Publish SDK helper vX.Y.1 (JS/Python) with example migration snippet.
- Prepare Dedicated/Private image build pipeline and notify SEs.

If anything urgent appears (customer regression >3 customers or clear data loss), escalate to CTO and trigger rollback.
